questions.explanation: Both labetalol and carvedilol are non-selective beta-blockers with additional alpha1 blocking activity, causing vasodilatation.
questions.keyConcept: Labetalol and carvedilol add alpha1 blockade for vasodilatation.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Non-selective beta blockers with a vasodilator effect due to alpha blockade:
questions.explanation: Both labetalol and carvedilol combine beta blockade with alpha-1 blockade, producing vasodilation.
questions.keyConcept: Labetalol and carvedilol add alpha-blocking vasodilation.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Regarding alpha adrenoceptor blockers, the following is not true:
options: Doxazosin is long acting with less first-dose hypotension
Tamsulosin is a selective alpha1A agonist used to improve symptoms of benign prostatic hyperplasia
Postural hypotension is a common adverse effect especially in the elderly
They cause miosis and nasal stuffiness
questions.explanation: Tamsulosin is a selective alpha1A antagonist (blocker), not an agonist, so this statement is untrue.
questions.keyConcept: Tamsulosin is an alpha1A blocker used in BPH.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Regarding prazosin, the following is not true:
options: It is used in benign prostatic hyperplasia
Doxazosin is preferred as it is longer acting with less first-dose hypotension
Tamsulosin is preferred in benign prostatic hyperplasia as it acts on α1A rather than α1B receptors, causing minimal change in blood pressure
questions.explanation: α1 blockers such as prazosin cause miosis (not mydriasis) because blocking α1 receptors on the radial pupillary muscle prevents dilation. The other statements are correct.
questions.keyConcept: α1 blockers cause miosis and nasal stuffiness, not mydriasis.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Regarding prazosin, the following is not true:
options: It is used in benign prostatic hyperplasia
Doxazosin is preferred to it as it is longer acting with less 1st dose hypotension
Tamsulosin is preferred to it in benign prostatic hyperplasia as it induces minimal change in BP as it acts on α1A not α1B receptors
questions.explanation: α1-blockade by prazosin causes miosis (and can cause floppy iris), not mydriasis, so D is untrue.
questions.keyConcept: α1-blockers cause miosis, not mydriasis.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Salbutamol replaced epinephrine in the treatment of bronchial asthma because:
options: Longer duration of action since it is not metabolized by MAO or COMT
No cardiac complications at regular doses
Can be given by many routes
questions.explanation: Salbutamol is longer acting (resistant to MAO/COMT), beta-2 selective with fewer cardiac effects, and available by multiple routes.
questions.keyConcept: Salbutamol is longer-acting, beta-2 selective and versatile.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The beta-mediated antihypertensive effects of bisoprolol (cardio-selective beta blocker) do not include:
questions.explanation: Skeletal muscle vasodilation is a beta-2 effect not produced by a cardio-selective beta-1 blocker, so it is not part of its action.
questions.keyConcept: Cardio-selective blockers do not cause beta-2 vasodilation.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The beta-mediated antihypertensive effects of bisoprolol (cardioselective blocker) do not include:
questions.explanation: Vasodilatation of skeletal blood vessels is a beta2-mediated effect, which the beta1-selective bisoprolol does not significantly produce.
questions.keyConcept: Cardioselective blockers spare beta2-mediated skeletal vasodilatation.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following adverse effect of beta blockers is not due to beta-1 blockade:
questions.explanation: Prolonged recovery from hypoglycemia results from beta-2 blockade impairing glycogenolysis; bradycardia, heart failure and AV block are beta-1 effects.
questions.keyConcept: Hypoglycemia prolongation is a beta-2, not beta-1, effect.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following adverse effect of beta blockers is not due to beta-1 blockade:
questions.explanation: Prolonged recovery from hypoglycemia is mediated by beta-2 blockade; bradycardia, heart failure and hypotension are beta-1 effects.
questions.keyConcept: Hypoglycemia prolongation is a beta-2 effect.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following adverse effect of beta blockers is not due to beta-2 blockade:
questions.explanation: Hypotension reflects beta-1 blockade reducing cardiac output; bronchospasm, prolonged hypoglycemia and cold extremities are beta-2 effects.
questions.keyConcept: Hypotension is a beta-1, not beta-2, blockade effect.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following adverse effect of beta-blockers is not mainly due to beta2 blockade:
questions.explanation: Bronchospasm, prolonged hypoglycaemia and cold extremities are beta2-blockade effects, whereas hypotension is a general beta-blocker effect not specifically tied to beta2 blockade.
questions.keyConcept: Hypotension is a general beta-blocker effect, not a beta2-specific one.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following adverse effect of β blockers is not due to β-1 blockade:
questions.explanation: Masking/prolongation of insulin-induced hypoglycemia is a β2 effect; bradycardia, heart failure and lipid changes relate to β1 blockade.
questions.keyConcept: Prolonged hypoglycemia from β-blockers is a β2 effect.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following adverse effect of β blockers is not due to β-1 blockade:
questions.explanation: Prolongation/masking of insulin-induced hypoglycemia is a β2 effect; the others relate to β1 blockade.
questions.keyConcept: Prolonged hypoglycemia is a β2-mediated β-blocker effect.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following adverse effect of β blockers is not due to β2 blockade:
questions.explanation: Bronchospasm, prolonged hypoglycemia and cold extremities are β2-blockade effects; hypotension is not a β2-blockade adverse effect.
questions.keyConcept: Bronchospasm, cold extremities and prolonged hypoglycemia are β2 effects.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following adverse effect of β blockers is not due to β2 blockade:
questions.explanation: Bronchospasm, prolonged hypoglycemia and cold extremities are β2-blockade effects; hypotension is not.
questions.keyConcept: Bronchospasm, cold extremities and prolonged hypoglycemia are β2 effects.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following adverse effects are seen with both methyldopa and clonidine:
questions.explanation: Sedation and dry mouth are common central adverse effects shared by both methyldopa and clonidine.
questions.keyConcept: Central alpha2 agonists share sedation and dry mouth.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following agent does not act on α1-receptors:
questions.explanation: Dobutamine is a selective β1 agonist with no significant α1 activity. Tamsulosin is an α1 blocker, carvedilol and labetalol block α1 (and β), and dopamine activates α1 at high doses.
questions.keyConcept: Dobutamine is β1-selective and does not act on α1 receptors.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following agent does not stimulate beta-1 receptors:
questions.explanation: Dopexamine acts on beta-2 and dopamine receptors with little beta-1 activity, so it does not appreciably stimulate beta-1.
questions.keyConcept: Dopexamine has minimal beta-1 activity.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following agent does not stimulate beta-2 receptors:
questions.explanation: Dobutamine is essentially beta-1 selective and lacks meaningful beta-2 agonism, unlike ritodrine, celiprolol and dopexamine.
questions.keyConcept: Dobutamine is beta-1 selective, not a beta-2 agonist.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following agent/s is/are a prodrug:
questions.explanation: Midodrine is converted to active desglymidodrine, and α-methyldopa is metabolized to α-methyl-noradrenaline (a false transmitter). Clonidine and pseudoephedrine are active as given.
questions.keyConcept: Midodrine and α-methyldopa are adrenergic prodrugs.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following difference/s between propranolol and other beta-blockers is/are true:
options: Betaxolol has no membrane-stabilizing activity, so it is preferred in glaucoma as it does not cause corneal anesthesia
Pindolol has intrinsic sympathomimetic activity, causes less bradycardia and is preferred in hypertensives with a low resting heart rate, but not in angina
Carvedilol has vasodilator and antioxidant effects, useful in hypertension and chronic heart failure
Bisoprolol is cardioselective with less risk of Raynaud phenomenon and less delay in recovery from hypoglycemia
questions.explanation: All statements correctly contrast newer beta-blockers with propranolol: betaxolol lacks membrane-stabilizing activity (safe in glaucoma), pindolol has ISA (avoided in angina), carvedilol is a vasodilating antioxidant (heart failure), and cardioselective bisoprolol causes less Raynaud and less hypoglycemia masking.
questions.keyConcept: Beta-blockers differ in cardioselectivity, ISA, membrane-stabilizing activity, and vasodilation.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following difference/s between propranolol & other β-blockers is/are True:
options: Propranolol has membrane-stabilizing activity, thus not preferred in glaucoma as it induces corneal anesthesia
Metoprolol is lipophilic with less bioavailability and more CNS side effects
Carvedilol has vasodilator, useful in hypertension & in chronic heart failure
Bisoprolol is cardio selective with less risk of Raynaud's phenomenon and less delay in recovery from hypoglycemia
questions.explanation: Each statement correctly describes a distinguishing property, so all of the above are true.
questions.keyConcept: Distinguishing pharmacology of propranolol, metoprolol, carvedilol and bisoprolol.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following difference/s between propranolol & other β-blockers is/are True:
options: Betaxolol has no membrane-stabilizing activity, thus preferred in glaucoma as it does not induce corneal anesthesia
Pindolol has intrinsic sympathomimetic activity, induces less bradycardia thus preferred in hypertensives with low resting heart rate, but not in angina
Carvedilol has vasodilator & antioxidant effects, useful in hypertension & in chronic heart failure
Bisoprolol is cardioselective with less risk of Raynaud's phenomenon and less delay in recovery from hypoglycemia
questions.explanation: Each statement correctly distinguishes a β-blocker property, so all of the above are true.
questions.keyConcept: Distinguishing properties of betaxolol, pindolol, carvedilol and bisoprolol.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following drug induces significant tachycardia:
questions.explanation: Doxazosin, an alpha1 blocker, can cause reflex tachycardia, especially at the first dose.
questions.keyConcept: Alpha1 blockers like doxazosin cause reflex tachycardia.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following drug is not matched to its adverse effect:
options: Clonidine / rebound hypertension even on missing a single dose
Bisoprolol / rebound tachycardia and anginal pain on sudden withdrawal
Midodrine / rebound hypertension on sudden withdrawal
questions.explanation: Midodrine is an alpha1 agonist; its sudden withdrawal causes hypotension, not rebound hypertension, so this match is wrong.
questions.keyConcept: Midodrine withdrawal causes hypotension, not rebound hypertension.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following drugs increase the effect of noradrenaline except:
questions.explanation: Reserpine depletes vesicular noradrenaline stores, decreasing its effect, so it is the exception.
questions.keyConcept: Reserpine depletes NE stores and reduces its effect.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following indication of epinephrine is entirely due to its alpha effect:
options: To prolong the action of local anesthetics
questions.explanation: Both prolonging local anesthetic action and controlling epistaxis rely on alpha-mediated vasoconstriction.
questions.keyConcept: Vasoconstriction (alpha) prolongs LA action and stops epistaxis.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following is a wrong statement about epinephrine:
options: Used in asthma due to its alpha and beta agonistic effect
Lifesaving in anaphylactic shock due to its rapid action
Induces hypoglycemia due to its beta-2 agonistic effect
questions.explanation: Epinephrine causes hyperglycemia (via glycogenolysis and reduced insulin), not hypoglycemia, so this statement is wrong.
questions.keyConcept: Epinephrine causes hyperglycemia, not hypoglycemia.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following is a wrong statement about sympathomimetics:
options: Inhibition of vesicular uptake abolishes the effect of indirectly acting drugs
Inhibition of vesicular uptake decreases the effect of dual-acting drugs
A directly acting alpha-1 agonist induces reflex tachycardia
questions.explanation: An alpha-1 agonist raises blood pressure and triggers reflex bradycardia, not tachycardia, so this statement is wrong.
questions.keyConcept: Alpha-1 agonists cause reflex bradycardia.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following is/are not true concerning anti-anginal effects of beta-blockers:
options: Reduction in heart rate and myocardial contractility
Stimulation of lipolysis resulting in increased fatty acid utilisation
Coronary vasodilatation increasing myocardial O2 supply
questions.explanation: Beta-blockers reduce myocardial oxygen demand by decreasing heart rate, contractility and blood pressure; they do not stimulate lipolysis or cause coronary vasodilatation.
questions.keyConcept: Beta-blockers help angina by reducing oxygen demand, not by vasodilatation.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following is/are not true concerning anti-anginal effects of β-blockers:
options: Reduction in heart rate & myocardial contractility
Stimulation of lipolysis resulting in increased fatty acid utilization
Coronary vasodilation increasing myocardial O2 supply in vasospastic angina
questions.explanation: β-blockers reduce BP, rate and contractility (lowering O2 demand); they do not stimulate lipolysis and are harmful in vasospastic angina (no coronary vasodilation), so C and D are untrue.
questions.keyConcept: β-blockers reduce O2 demand; they do not vasodilate coronaries and are unsuitable for vasospastic angina.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following is/are not true concerning anti-anginal effects of β-blockers:
options: Reduction in heart rate & myocardial contractility
Inhibition of lipolysis resulting in decreased fatty acid utilization
questions.explanation: β-blockers do not produce coronary vasodilation and are actually harmful in vasospastic angina, so D is untrue.
questions.keyConcept: β-blockers are unsuitable for vasospastic angina (no coronary vasodilation).

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following is/are true concerning anti-arrhythmic effects of β-blockers:
options: Slow automaticity of sympathetically-induced ectopic focus
questions.explanation: β-blockers slow the SA node and AV conduction and suppress sympathetically driven ectopic automaticity — both statements are true.
questions.keyConcept: β-blockers slow SA/AV nodal activity and ectopic automaticity.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following is/are true concerning the anti-arrhythmic effects of beta-blockers:
options: Decrease SA node rate and AV node conduction
Slow the automaticity of a sympathetically-induced ectopic focus
questions.explanation: As class II antiarrhythmics, beta-blockers decrease SA node firing, slow AV nodal conduction, and suppress automaticity of ectopic foci driven by sympathetic stimulation.
questions.keyConcept: Beta-blockers (class II) slow SA/AV nodal activity and suppress sympathetic ectopy.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following is/are true concerning the anti-arrhythmic effects of beta-blockers:
options: Decrease SAN rate and AVN conduction
Slow automaticity of a sympathetically-induced ectopic focus
questions.explanation: Beta-blockers slow the sinoatrial rate and AV conduction and suppress automaticity of sympathetically driven ectopic foci.
questions.keyConcept: Beta-blockers slow SAN/AVN and ectopic automaticity.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following is incorrect regarding beta adrenergic receptor blockers:
options: Timolol (lipophilic without membrane-stabilizing activity) is suitable for glaucoma
Metoprolol (cardio-selective) has less hypoglycemia, bronchospasm and peripheral vasospasm
Atenolol (hydrophilic cardio-selective) is effective in treatment of thyrotoxicosis
Propranolol (non-selective lipophilic) is used in essential tremors
questions.explanation: Thyrotoxicosis is best controlled by non-selective propranolol, which also blocks peripheral T4-to-T3 conversion; hydrophilic cardio-selective atenolol is less effective, so this statement is incorrect.
questions.keyConcept: Propranolol, not atenolol, is preferred in thyrotoxicosis.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following is incorrect regarding beta adrenergic receptors:
options: Timolol (lipophilic without membrane stabilising) is suitable for glaucoma
Metoprolol (cardioselective) has less insulin-induced hypoglycaemia, less bronchospasm and less peripheral vasospasm
Atenolol (hydrophilic cardioselective) is effective in treatment of thyrotoxicosis
Propranolol (nonselective lipophilic) is used in treatment of essential tremors
Nebivolol (cardioselective vasodilator) is not effective in angina as it does not induce significant bradycardia
questions.explanation: Atenolol is hydrophilic and primarily eliminated by the kidneys, making it less effective in thyrotoxicosis, so this statement is incorrect.
questions.keyConcept: Hydrophilic atenolol is less suited to thyrotoxicosis than lipophilic blockers.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following is not a pharmacological effect of directly acting beta receptor agonists:
options: Relax smooth muscle of the bronchi
questions.explanation: Beta agonists increase heart rate (positive chronotropy); decreasing heart rate is not a beta-agonist effect.
questions.keyConcept: Beta agonists increase, not decrease, heart rate.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following is not a shared adverse effect between dopamine and dobutamine:
questions.explanation: Dopamine raises blood pressure at higher doses via alpha effects, whereas dobutamine has little effect on blood pressure, so hypertension is not shared.
questions.keyConcept: Hypertension is a dopamine, not dobutamine, effect.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following is not a therapeutic use due to blocking of beta1 receptors:
questions.explanation: Per the answer key, open angle glaucoma is taken as the exception here, while the other uses follow directly from beta1 blockade.
questions.keyConcept: Hypertension, IHD and HOCM are core beta1-blockade uses.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following is not an adverse effect of alpha blockers:
questions.explanation: Cold extremities and muscle cramps are characteristic of beta-blockers (beta2 blockade), not alpha-blockers.
questions.keyConcept: Cold extremities are a beta-blocker, not alpha-blocker, effect.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following is not an adverse effect of α blockers:
questions.explanation: Hypertriglyceridaemia is associated with β-blockers, not α-blockers (which actually improve lipids); the others are recognized α-blocker effects.
questions.keyConcept: Dyslipidemia (↑triglycerides) is a β-blocker effect, not an α-blocker effect.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following is not an adverse effect of salbutamol (beta-2 agonist):
questions.explanation: Salbutamol drives potassium into cells, causing hypokalemia, not hyperkalemia, so this is not an adverse effect.
questions.keyConcept: Beta-2 agonists cause hypokalemia, not hyperkalemia.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following is not an indication for hydrophilic beta blockers:
questions.explanation: Per the answer key, thyrotoxicosis is taken as the exception; hydrophilic beta-blockers are mainly used in hypertension, ischaemic heart disease and HOCM.
questions.keyConcept: Hydrophilic beta-blockers are less central-acting for thyrotoxicosis.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following is not an indication for indirect sympathomimetics:
questions.explanation: Sympathomimetics raise blood pressure and are used for hypotensive states, not hypertension.
questions.keyConcept: Sympathomimetics treat hypotension, not hypertension.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following is not an indication for propranolol:
questions.explanation: Propranolol is not used topically for simple glaucoma; topical agents such as timolol are preferred.
questions.keyConcept: Propranolol is not a topical glaucoma treatment.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following is not an indication for using labetalol:
questions.explanation: Labetalol is not typically used for HOCM, unlike its established roles in eclampsia, phaeochromocytoma, clonidine rebound and aortic dissection.
questions.keyConcept: Labetalol is not indicated for HOCM.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following is not an indication of salbutamol (beta-2 agonist):
questions.explanation: Salbutamol causes beta-2 vasodilation, which would worsen postural hypotension rather than treat it.
questions.keyConcept: Beta-2 vasodilation worsens postural hypotension.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following is not true concerning the anti-anginal effects of beta-blockers:
options: Reduction in heart rate and myocardial contractility
Stimulation of lipolysis increasing fatty acid utilization
Coronary vasodilation increasing myocardial O2 supply in vasospastic angina
questions.explanation: Beta-blockers inhibit (not stimulate) lipolysis and can worsen vasospastic angina via unopposed coronary constriction, so both C and D are untrue.
questions.keyConcept: Beta-blockers reduce demand; they are unhelpful in vasospastic angina.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following is not true regarding nebivolol:
options: Not used in ischaemic heart disease
questions.explanation: Nebivolol is associated with less sexual dysfunction than other beta-blockers, so this statement is untrue.
questions.keyConcept: Nebivolol causes less sexual dysfunction than other beta-blockers.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following is wrong about propranolol:
options: Short-acting non-selective beta blocker with local anesthetic effect
Decreases portal blood pressure by its beta-1 and beta-2 blocking effects
Decreases IOP and is used locally in treatment of glaucoma
questions.explanation: Propranolol has membrane-stabilizing (local anesthetic) activity and would anesthetize the cornea, so it is not used topically for glaucoma; timolol is preferred.
questions.keyConcept: Propranolol's local anesthetic activity precludes topical eye use.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following is wrong about propranolol:
options: Short acting non-selective beta blocker with local anaesthetic (membrane-stabilising) effect
Decreases portal blood pressure by its beta1 and beta2 blocking effects
Decreases IOP and is used locally in treatment of glaucoma
questions.explanation: Propranolol lowers intraocular pressure systemically but is not used topically for glaucoma; timolol is preferred.
questions.keyConcept: Propranolol is not a topical glaucoma agent.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following statement about alpha blockers is incorrect:
options: Doxazosin is long acting with less first-dose hypotension
Tamsulosin is a selective alpha1A agonist used in BPH
Phenoxybenzamine is a prodrug used in phaeochromocytoma emergency
Labetalol is a nonselective beta blocker and alpha1 blocker used in hypertension
questions.explanation: Tamsulosin is a selective alpha1A antagonist used in BPH, not an agonist, so this statement is incorrect.
questions.keyConcept: Tamsulosin is an alpha1A antagonist, not an agonist.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The β-mediated antihypertensive effects of bisoprolol do not include:
questions.explanation: Bisoprolol lowers BP via reduced renin, baroreceptor resetting and negative inotropy/chronotropy; it does not cause skeletal-muscle vasodilatation (that would need β2 agonism).
questions.keyConcept: β-blocker antihypertensive mechanisms do not include vasodilatation.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Vasodilator Beta blockers include:
questions.explanation: Labetalol and carvedilol have additional α-blocking activity producing vasodilatation.
questions.keyConcept: Labetalol and carvedilol are the vasodilating β-blockers.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Vasodilator beta blockers include:
questions.explanation: Labetalol and carvedilol have additional alpha-1 blocking activity producing vasodilation.
questions.keyConcept: Labetalol and carvedilol are vasodilating beta-blockers.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: When a patient is taking an adrenergic drug, the nurse expects to observe which effect?
questions.explanation: Adrenergic drugs activate the sympathetic nervous system, leading to effects such as increased heart rate.
questions.keyConcept: Adrenergic stimulation increases heart rate.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Which of the following is not a shared character between carvedilol and labetalol?
questions.explanation: Carvedilol is used in heart failure whereas labetalol is not, so this is the character they do not share.
questions.keyConcept: Only carvedilol (not labetalol) is used in heart failure.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Compare and contrast between dopamine and dobutamine (mention 3 differences).
questions.modelAnswer: 1) Receptors: dopamine acts on D1, beta1 and alpha1 (dose-dependent) while dobutamine is primarily beta1. 2) Renal blood flow: dopamine increases it via D1 at low doses while dobutamine has no significant D1 effect. 3) Arrhythmogenicity: dopamine is more arrhythmogenic, especially at higher doses, while dobutamine is less arrhythmogenic. Dopamine is preferred in cardiogenic shock with renal dysfunction.
questions.explanation: Dobutamine is a focused beta1 inotrope; dopamine has broader dose-dependent actions.
questions.keyConcept: Dopamine is multi-receptor and dose-dependent; dobutamine is mainly beta1.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Compare between dopamine and dobutamine regarding the adverse effects.
questions.modelAnswer: Dopamine causes D1-mediated headache, nausea and vomiting, beta-1-mediated anginal pain and arrhythmia, and alpha-1-mediated hypertension and gangrene. Dobutamine has no D1 effect, is less arrhythmogenic through its beta-1 action, and has no alpha-1 effect.
questions.keyConcept: Dopamine has more diverse adverse effects; dobutamine is less arrhythmogenic and lacks alpha/D1 effects.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Compare between dopamine and dobutamine regarding the mechanism of action.
questions.modelAnswer: Dopamine is a D1 agonist at low dose, a beta-1 agonist at moderate dose and an alpha-1 agonist at high dose. Dobutamine has no D1 effect, acts as a beta-1 agonist and has no alpha-1 agonist effect.
questions.keyConcept: Dopamine has dose-dependent D1/beta-1/alpha-1 actions; dobutamine is essentially beta-1.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Compare between dopamine and dobutamine regarding the therapeutic uses.
questions.modelAnswer: Dopamine is used in acute heart failure and cardiogenic shock especially with renal impairment or hypotension, and short-term in chronic refractory heart failure. Dobutamine is used in acute heart failure and cardiogenic shock especially in normotensive patients with normal renal function, and short-term in chronic refractory heart failure.
questions.keyConcept: Dopamine suits shock with renal impairment/hypotension; dobutamine suits normotensive patients.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Dipivefrine (pro-epinephrine) is used instead of epinephrine in the treatment of open-angle glaucoma. Explain.
questions.modelAnswer: Epinephrine itself is unstable and destroyed in an alkaline medium; dipivefrine is a more stable lipophilic prodrug that penetrates the cornea better and is then converted to active epinephrine.
questions.keyConcept: Dipivefrine is a stable, better-penetrating prodrug of epinephrine.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Enumerate the advantages of selective beta-2 agonists over non-selective ones.
questions.modelAnswer: Selective beta-2 agonists cause no cardiac adverse effects at therapeutic doses, are longer acting and are available by all routes including the oral route.
questions.keyConcept: Selective beta-2 agonists are cardiac-sparing, longer acting and orally available.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Enumerate the drugs affecting the enzymatic degradation of norepinephrine, mentioning their uses.
questions.modelAnswer: Monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOIs) are used in depression and parkinsonism, and catechol-O-methyltransferase inhibitors (COMT inhibitors) are used in parkinsonism.
questions.keyConcept: MAOIs (depression, parkinsonism) and COMT inhibitors (parkinsonism) block norepinephrine degradation.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Enumerate the drugs that interfere with the uptake of catecholamines, mentioning their proposed mechanism.
questions.modelAnswer: Uptake I actively transports norepinephrine from the synaptic cleft into the neuronal cytoplasm (to be stored in granules or metabolized by MAO) and is blocked by tricyclic antidepressants and cocaine. Vesicular uptake moves norepinephrine from the cytoplasm into storage vesicles and is blocked by reserpine (which depletes stores). Uptake II carries catecholamines into target organs for metabolism and is blocked by glucocorticoids.
questions.keyConcept: Uptake I is blocked by TCAs/cocaine, vesicular uptake by reserpine, uptake II by glucocorticoids.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Enumerate the therapeutic uses of ephedrine.
questions.modelAnswer: Ephedrine is used for epistaxis, as a nasal decongestant, in spinal shock, for nocturnal enuresis in children and for urinary incontinence in adults.
questions.keyConcept: Ephedrine treats epistaxis, congestion, spinal shock, enuresis and incontinence.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Epinephrine is used in anaphylactic shock. Explain.
questions.modelAnswer: Epinephrine reverses the bronchospasm and hypotension of anaphylaxis, making it lifesaving.
questions.keyConcept: Epinephrine reverses anaphylactic bronchospasm and hypotension.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Explain the mechanism of the cheese reaction.
questions.modelAnswer: Because MAO is inhibited, dietary tyramine escapes intestinal first-pass metabolism, enters the circulation and triggers release of norepinephrine from neurons that are loaded with norepinephrine, producing a hypertensive crisis.
questions.keyConcept: Tyramine escapes metabolism and releases stored norepinephrine when MAO is inhibited.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: List four contraindications of sympathomimetics (e.g. adrenaline).
questions.modelAnswer: Phaeochromocytoma (risk of hypertensive crisis); hypertension (risk of exacerbation); hyperthyroidism (increased sensitivity, risk of arrhythmias); ischaemic heart disease (increased myocardial oxygen demand, angina, arrhythmias); general anaesthesia with sensitising agents (arrhythmia risk).
questions.explanation: Sympathomimetics are avoided where adrenergic stimulation would be dangerous.
questions.keyConcept: Sympathomimetics are contraindicated where adrenergic drive is harmful.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: List four therapeutic uses of adrenaline.
questions.modelAnswer: Anaphylactic shock (reverses bronchospasm and hypotension); cardiac arrest (restore rhythm); adjunct to local anaesthetics (prolong action, reduce bleeding); topical haemostasis (e.g. epistaxis).
questions.explanation: Adrenaline's broad receptor activity gives it several emergency uses.
questions.keyConcept: Adrenaline is used in anaphylaxis, arrest, anaesthesia and haemostasis.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: List the adverse effects of selective beta-2 agonists.
questions.modelAnswer: They can cause anxiety and restlessness, headache and tremors, hypokalemia, tachycardia, hypoxemia and tolerance.
questions.keyConcept: Beta-2 agonists cause tremor, hypokalemia, tachycardia and tolerance.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: List the indications of beta-2 agonists, mentioning two preparations.
questions.modelAnswer: They are used in bronchial asthma (salbutamol, short-acting; salmeterol, long-acting), to prevent premature labor and threatened abortion (terbutaline and ritodrine) and in peripheral vascular disease (salbutamol).
questions.keyConcept: Beta-2 agonists treat asthma, premature labor and peripheral vascular disease.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: List the main metabolic effects of adrenaline injection.
questions.modelAnswer: Hyperglycaemia: beta2 stimulation (increased hepatic glycogenolysis, decreased insulin release) plus alpha1 inhibition of insulin release. Hypokalaemia: beta2 stimulation enhancing cellular uptake of potassium. Increased lipolysis: beta1 and beta3 stimulation raising free fatty acids.
questions.explanation: Adrenaline mobilises glucose and fat while shifting potassium intracellularly.
questions.keyConcept: Adrenaline causes hyperglycaemia, hypokalaemia and lipolysis.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: List the main metabolic effects of an epinephrine injection.
questions.modelAnswer: Epinephrine causes hepatic glycogenolysis (mainly beta-2 with alpha-1), inhibits insulin release (alpha-2 dominant) while stimulating it through beta-2, promotes lipolysis (beta-2/beta-3, inhibited by alpha-2) and stimulates renin release (beta-1).
questions.keyConcept: Epinephrine raises blood glucose via glycogenolysis, modulates insulin, and promotes lipolysis and renin release.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: List the possible adverse effects of phenylephrine.
questions.modelAnswer: Phenylephrine can cause hypertension and reflex bradycardia, and with local application rebound nasal congestion and atrophic rhinitis.
questions.keyConcept: Phenylephrine causes hypertension, reflex bradycardia and rebound congestion.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: List the therapeutic uses and adverse effects of beta2 agonists.
questions.modelAnswer: Therapeutic uses: bronchial asthma (bronchodilation), prevention of premature labour/threatened abortion (uterine relaxation). Adverse effects: tremors, anxiety, restlessness, palpitations, reflex tachycardia, hypokalaemia, increased glucose levels.
questions.explanation: Beta2 agonists relax smooth muscle but spill over to skeletal, cardiac and metabolic effects.
questions.keyConcept: Beta2 agonists relax bronchi and uterus with tremor and metabolic side effects.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: List the therapeutic uses and possible adverse effects of phenylephrine.
questions.modelAnswer: Therapeutic uses: fundus examination (mydriasis), nasal decongestant (vasoconstriction), management of chronic postural hypotension, paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia (via reflex bradycardia). Adverse effects: hypertension (vasoconstriction), reflex bradycardia, headache, rebound nasal congestion with prolonged topical use.
questions.explanation: Phenylephrine is a selective alpha1 agonist, so its actions stem from vasoconstriction.
questions.keyConcept: Phenylephrine's effects all derive from alpha1 vasoconstriction.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: List the therapeutic uses of epinephrine.
questions.modelAnswer: Epinephrine is used for anaphylactic shock, asthma associated with locked lung, cardiac arrest, to arrest bleeding, added to local anesthetics to prolong their action, and in open-angle glaucoma to lower intraocular pressure.
questions.keyConcept: Epinephrine treats anaphylaxis, cardiac arrest, bleeding and prolongs local anesthesia.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: List the therapeutic uses of phenylephrine.
questions.modelAnswer: Phenylephrine is used as a mydriatic for fundus examination, as an eye and nasal decongestant, to raise blood pressure in hypotensive states, in paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia associated with marked hypotension (raising BP triggers reflex vagal stimulation) and as a local treatment for hemorrhoids.
questions.keyConcept: Phenylephrine is a mydriatic, decongestant and pressor agent.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: List therapeutic uses of adrenaline and the possible receptors involved in each use.
questions.modelAnswer: Anaphylactic shock (lifesaving): alpha1 vasoconstriction, beta1 cardiac stimulation, beta2 bronchodilation. Cardiac arrest: beta1 cardiac stimulation to restore rhythm. Prolonging local anaesthetics: alpha1 local vasoconstriction reducing systemic absorption. Topical haemostatic (e.g. epistaxis): alpha1 vasoconstriction to stop bleeding.
questions.explanation: Each therapeutic use of adrenaline reflects a specific adrenergic receptor action.
questions.keyConcept: Adrenaline's uses map to distinct alpha and beta receptor effects.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: List three uses of indirect sympathomimetics (amphetamine).
questions.modelAnswer: Narcolepsy (to promote wakefulness); Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (to improve focus); Obesity (as an appetite suppressant).
questions.explanation: Amphetamine's central stimulation underlies all three uses.
questions.keyConcept: Amphetamine is used for narcolepsy, ADHD and obesity.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Mention four cardiovascular uses of sympathomimetics with examples.
questions.modelAnswer: Shock (cardiogenic, septic): dopamine, noradrenaline to raise blood pressure and cardiac output. Cardiac arrest: adrenaline to stimulate cardiac activity. Acute heart failure: dobutamine to increase contractility. Hypertension during surgery/emergencies: phenylephrine to raise BP via vasoconstriction. Orthostatic hypotension: midodrine.
questions.explanation: Different sympathomimetics are chosen for their receptor selectivity in cardiovascular conditions.
questions.keyConcept: Sympathomimetics treat shock, arrest, heart failure and hypotension.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Mention the contraindications of sympathomimetics.
questions.modelAnswer: Sympathomimetics are contraindicated in patients taking beta blockers, in hypertension and in thyrotoxicosis, and epinephrine should be avoided with local anesthetics in cardiac patients.
questions.keyConcept: Avoid sympathomimetics in beta-blockade, hypertension, thyrotoxicosis and (with LA) cardiac patients.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Mention the therapeutic use of dopexamine.
questions.modelAnswer: Dopexamine is used in shock with low cardiac output and peripheral vasoconstriction, for example after myocardial infarction or cardiac surgery.
questions.keyConcept: Dopexamine treats low-output shock with peripheral vasoconstriction.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Mention the therapeutic uses of dopamine and their relation to its dose.
questions.modelAnswer: Low dose (D1 stimulation): selective renal and mesenteric vasodilatation, increasing renal blood flow and urine output. Moderate dose (beta1 stimulation): cardiac stimulation (positive inotropic and chronotropic effects) used in cardiogenic shock. High dose (alpha1 stimulation): general vasoconstriction and increased blood pressure used in severe shock.
questions.explanation: Dopamine's receptor activation is dose-dependent.
questions.keyConcept: Dopamine's effects shift from D1 to beta1 to alpha1 as the dose rises.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Mention the therapeutic uses of norepinephrine.
questions.modelAnswer: Norepinephrine is used in the treatment of shock (septic and cardiogenic), shock with pulmonary embolism and hypotension after removal of a pheochromocytoma.
questions.keyConcept: Norepinephrine is a pressor used for septic/cardiogenic shock and post-pheochromocytoma hypotension.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Mention three cardiovascular uses of sympathomimetics with examples.
questions.modelAnswer: They are used in chronic refractory heart failure and in acute heart failure or cardiogenic shock after acute myocardial infarction or open-heart surgery (dopamine acting on beta-1 and D1 with renal vasodilation, and dobutamine); in anaphylactic shock (epinephrine: alpha-1 vasoconstriction, beta-1 raising cardiac output, beta-2 bronchodilation); and in heart block (isoprenaline).
questions.keyConcept: Sympathomimetics treat heart failure/shock, anaphylaxis and heart block.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Patients taking MAOIs may have some drug interactions. Explain.
questions.modelAnswer: They may develop the cheese reaction, a hypertensive crisis caused by eating a diet rich in tyramine such as fermented foods (e.g., blue cheese).
questions.keyConcept: MAOIs cause the tyramine (cheese) reaction, a hypertensive crisis.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Phenylephrine is preferred to atropine substitutes as a mydriatic for fundus examination. Explain.
questions.modelAnswer: Phenylephrine produces mydriasis without cycloplegia, which is especially advantageous in patients with glaucoma.
questions.keyConcept: Phenylephrine dilates the pupil without cycloplegia.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: What are the adverse effects of indirect sympathomimetics?
questions.modelAnswer: They cause marked CNS stimulation (hallucinations, psychosis, convulsions and dependence on prolonged use), marked cardiovascular stimulation (palpitation, arrhythmia, hypertension) and marked anorexia; the newer anorexigens can cause pulmonary hypertension and valvular heart disease.
questions.keyConcept: Indirect sympathomimetics cause CNS and cardiovascular stimulation, anorexia and (anorexigens) cardiopulmonary damage.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Cross match each drug to its mechanism of action.

pairs.premise: Splanchnic vasodilator activating β2, D1 and D2 receptors

questions.explanation: Dobutamine is a selective β1 agonist; dopexamine activates β2, D1 and D2; fenoldopam is a selective D1 agonist (hypertensive crisis); midodrine is an α1 vasopressor.
questions.keyConcept: Receptor targets of dobutamine, dopexamine, fenoldopam, and midodrine.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Cross match each drug to its mechanism of action:

pairs.premise: Splanchnic vasodilator that activates β2, D1 & D2 receptors
Peripheral vasodilator that activates D-1 receptor

questions.explanation: Dobutamine is a β1 inotrope; dopexamine activates β2 and dopaminergic receptors; fenoldopam is a D1 vasodilator; midodrine is an α1 vasopressor.
questions.keyConcept: Receptor mechanisms of dobutamine, dopexamine, fenoldopam and midodrine.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Cross match each drug to its mechanism of action and use:

pairs.target: Vasopressor that activates α1 receptor used in postural hypotension
Central α2 receptor agonist used in pregnant hypertensive patients
Peripheral vasodilator that activates D1 receptor used in hypertensive crisis
Central α2- and imidazoline receptor agonist used in hypertensive urgency
Long acting β2 agonist used in asthma

questions.explanation: Midodrine = α1 vasopressor (postural hypotension); methyldopa = central α2 agonist in pregnancy; fenoldopam = D1 vasodilator (hypertensive crisis); clonidine = central α2/imidazoline agonist; salmeterol = long-acting β2 agonist.
questions.keyConcept: Mechanisms and uses of midodrine, methyldopa, fenoldopam, clonidine and salmeterol.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Cross match each sympathomimetic to its hemodynamic effect.

pairs.target: Marked increase in blood pressure with reflex bradycardia
Decreases diastolic and mean blood pressure and increases heart rate
Increases mean blood pressure and increases heart rate
Prodrug; increases blood pressure with reflex vagal bradycardia

questions.explanation: Norepinephrine (α1+β1) raises BP markedly with reflex bradycardia; isoprenaline (β1+β2) lowers diastolic/mean BP and raises rate; epinephrine raises mean BP and rate; midodrine (α1 prodrug) raises BP with reflex bradycardia.
questions.keyConcept: Hemodynamic profiles follow adrenergic receptor selectivity.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Cross match each sympathomimetic to its hemodynamic/pharmacologic profile.

pairs.target: Increases blood pressure with reflex vagal bradycardia
Renal vasodilator, positive inotrope and chronotrope, with vasopressor effects at high dose
Positive inotrope with minimal effect on blood pressure or heart rate
Weak positive inotrope and powerful splanchnic vasodilator

questions.explanation: Phenylephrine (pure α1) raises BP with reflex bradycardia; dopamine is dose-dependent (D1 renal vasodilation → β1 → α1 vasopressor); dobutamine (β1) is mainly inotropic; dopexamine (β2+D1) is a weak inotrope and splanchnic vasodilator.
questions.keyConcept: Dose- and receptor-dependent hemodynamics of dopaminergic/adrenergic agonists.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Cross match each sympathomimetic to its therapeutic use.

pairs.target: β2 agonist used in premature labor / threatened abortion

questions.explanation: Terbutaline/ritodrine (β2) relax the uterus; epinephrine (α) is a local hemostatic; oxymetazoline (α) is a topical decongestant; pseudoephedrine (mixed) is a systemic decongestant.
questions.keyConcept: Therapeutic uses of selective and mixed sympathomimetics.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Cross match the following adrenergic drug classes to their indications:

pairs.target: Chronic refractory HF / acute HF / cardiogenic shock

questions.explanation: β2 agonists treat asthma and tocolysis; β1 agonists support failing hearts; α1 agonists are decongestant/mydriatic; central α2 agonists lower blood pressure.
questions.keyConcept: Indications mapped to adrenergic receptor-agonist classes.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Cross-match the following adrenergic drugs to their indications.

pairs.target: Chronic refractory HF / acute HF / cardiogenic shock

questions.explanation: Beta1 agonists stimulate the failing heart; beta2 agonists relax bronchi and uterus; alpha1 agonists cause mydriasis and conjunctival decongestion; central alpha2 agonists lower blood pressure.
questions.keyConcept: Adrenergic agonists are used according to their receptor selectivity.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Cross-match the following drugs with their possible indication.

pairs.target: Cardiogenic shock with intact kidney function

questions.explanation: Dobutamine supports the heart in cardiogenic shock; ephedrine is used for enuresis; salbutamol relieves acute asthma; midodrine raises blood pressure in postural hypotension.
questions.keyConcept: Sympathomimetics are matched to indications by receptor profile.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Cross match the following inotrope/vasoactive sympathomimetics to their hemodynamic effects:

pairs.target: Increase blood pressure with reflex vagal bradycardia
Renal vasodilator, positive inotrope & chronotrope with vasopressor effects in high dose
Positive inotrope, minimal effect on blood pressure or heart rate
Weak positive inotrope; powerful splanchnic vasodilator

questions.explanation: Phenylephrine (α1) raises BP with reflex bradycardia; dopamine is dose-dependent (renal vasodilation → inotropy → vasopressor); dobutamine is a β1 inotrope; dopexamine is a weak inotrope and splanchnic vasodilator.
questions.keyConcept: Hemodynamic profiles of phenylephrine, dopamine, dobutamine and dopexamine.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Cross match the following sympathomimetics to their hemodynamic effects:

pairs.target: Marked increase in blood pressure with reflex bradycardia
Decreases diastolic & mean blood pressure & increases heart rate
Increases mean blood pressure & increases heart rate
Prodrug, increases blood pressure with reflex vagal bradycardia

questions.explanation: NE (α1/β1) markedly raises BP with reflex bradycardia; isoprenaline (β1/β2) drops diastolic/mean BP and raises HR; epinephrine raises mean BP and HR; midodrine is an α1 prodrug raising BP with reflex bradycardia.
questions.keyConcept: Hemodynamic signatures of NE, isoprenaline, epinephrine and midodrine.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Cross match the following sympathomimetics to their uses:

pairs.target: Beta2 agonist in premature labor / threatened abortion

questions.explanation: Terbutaline/ritodrine are β2 tocolytics; epinephrine is a hemostatic vasoconstrictor; oxymetazoline is a topical α decongestant; pseudoephedrine is a dual-acting systemic decongestant.
questions.keyConcept: Therapeutic uses of terbutaline/ritodrine, epinephrine, oxymetazoline and pseudoephedrine.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: All the following drugs induce tachycardia except:
questions.explanation: Phenylephrine is a pure alpha1 agonist that causes vasoconstriction and a reflex bradycardia, so it does not induce tachycardia.
questions.keyConcept: Phenylephrine causes reflex bradycardia, not tachycardia.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: All the following regarding adrenaline is true except:
options: Should be avoided with beta blockers, thyrotoxicosis or ischaemic heart disease
Relaxation of the wall of the GIT by stimulation of alpha and beta receptors
No change in mean BP in therapeutic dose
questions.explanation: Adrenaline increases both systolic and diastolic blood pressure, raising mean BP, so 'no change' is incorrect.
questions.keyConcept: Adrenaline raises mean arterial pressure.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Alpha1 receptor agonist is not effective in treatment of:
questions.explanation: Alpha1 agonists cause vasoconstriction; ventricular tachycardia with hypotension requires increased contractility or rate, not vasoconstriction.
questions.keyConcept: Alpha1 agonists do not treat ventricular tachycardia.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Alpha1 receptor agonist should not be used in the following condition:
options: Fundus examination in patients with glaucoma
questions.explanation: Alpha1 agonists cause vasoconstriction and raise blood pressure, so they should not be used in a hypertensive state.
questions.keyConcept: Alpha1 agonists are contraindicated in hypertension.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Dobutamine differs from dopamine in all the following except:
options: Preferred in acute heart failure with renal dysfunction
Inotropic effect more than chronotropic effect
questions.explanation: Dobutamine is preferred in acute heart failure without renal dysfunction; dopamine is preferred when there is renal dysfunction, so this is the exception.
questions.keyConcept: Dopamine, not dobutamine, is preferred with renal dysfunction.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Dopamine is preferred to dobutamine in cardiogenic shock with hypotension or renal impairment because:
options: D-1 effect of dopamine induces renal vasodilation & increases renal blood flow
Beta-1 effect of dobutamine increases arrhythmia compared to dopamine
questions.explanation: Dopamine improves renal perfusion (D1) and supports BP via α vasopressor effect, making it preferable when hypotension/renal impairment coexist (A and B).
questions.keyConcept: Dopamine adds D1 renal vasodilation and α vasopressor support over dobutamine.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Dopamine is preferred to dobutamine in cardiogenic shock with hypotension or renal impairment because:
options: D1 stimulant effect of dopamine induces vasodilatation and increases renal blood flow
Dopamine induces an alpha-mediated vasopressor effect
Beta1 selective effect of dobutamine increases the risk of arrhythmia compared to dopamine
questions.explanation: Dopamine's D1 agonism increases renal blood flow while its alpha-mediated vasoconstriction supports blood pressure, making it useful in shock with renal impairment.
questions.keyConcept: Dopamine combines renal vasodilatation with vasopressor support.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Epinephrine induced hypokalemia is due to:
questions.explanation: Per the source key the answer is A+B. Note: epinephrine-induced hypokalemia is primarily due to β2-mediated cellular (skeletal muscle/hepatic) K+ uptake, so the option wording is pharmacologically imperfect — flag for review.
questions.keyConcept: Epinephrine causes β2-mediated cellular K+ uptake (item wording flagged).

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Epinephrine should be avoided in all of the following patients except:
questions.explanation: Per the source key, the exception is patients on alpha blockers. Note: epinephrine with a non-selective α-blocker can cause 'epinephrine reversal,' so this item is pharmacologically debatable — flag for review.
questions.keyConcept: Epinephrine is hazardous in thyrotoxic/diabetic/hypertensive/cardiac patients (item flagged).

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: In paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia with hypotension, reflex bradycardia may be induced by:
questions.explanation: Phenylephrine raises blood pressure by alpha1 vasoconstriction, triggering a reflex vagal bradycardia useful in PSVT with hypotension.
questions.keyConcept: Phenylephrine ends PSVT through reflex vagal bradycardia.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Metabolic actions of epinephrine include all of the following except:
options: Decreases serum K by B1 stimulation
Inhibition of Insulin secretion by B2
questions.explanation: Epinephrine inhibits insulin secretion via α2 (not β2), so C is the exception. Note: the K+ effect (option B) is actually β2-mediated, so that statement is also imperfectly worded — flag for review.
questions.keyConcept: Epinephrine inhibits insulin via α2 receptors (item has a secondary wording flaw on K+).

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Noradrenaline can be used in all the following types of shock except:
options: Cardiogenic with systolic blood pressure less than 70 mmHg
questions.explanation: Noradrenaline is not used in anaphylactic shock; adrenaline is preferred because of its beta2 effects.
questions.keyConcept: Adrenaline, not noradrenaline, is used in anaphylaxis.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Pharmacological actions of subcutaneous injection of adrenaline do not include:
options: Decrease renin release (beta1) decreasing serum potassium
questions.explanation: Adrenaline stimulates (not decreases) renin release via beta1 receptors, so this statement is the exception.
questions.keyConcept: Adrenaline increases beta1-mediated renin release.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Salbutamol replaced epinephrine in treatment of bronchial asthma because:
options: It seldom induces tremors or tolerance on long term use
Longer duration of action since it is not metabolized by MAO or COMT
No cardiac complications in regular doses
Can be given by many routes
questions.explanation: Salbutamol is β2-selective with a longer duration (not a MAO/COMT substrate), fewer cardiac effects and multiple routes — but it DOES cause tremor, so all are true except A.
questions.keyConcept: Salbutamol: selective β2 agonist, longer-acting than epinephrine but still causes tremor.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Selective beta2 agonists replaced adrenaline in treatment of bronchial asthma because of all the following except:
options: Longer duration of action since it is not metabolised by MAO or COMT
It seldom induces tremors or tolerance on long-term use
No cardiac complications in regular doses
Can be given by many routes
questions.explanation: Selective beta2 agonists can still cause tremors and tolerance on long-term use, so this is the exception.
questions.keyConcept: Beta2 agonists can still cause tremors and tolerance.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following adverse effect is not encountered with selective beta2 agonist:
options: Tolerance on long-term systemic use due to receptor down-regulation
questions.explanation: Selective beta2 agonists cause hypokalaemia (not hyperkalaemia), so this is the exception.
questions.keyConcept: Beta2 agonists cause hypokalaemia.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following adverse effects are seen with both methyl dopa & clonidine:
options: Sedation, dry mouth and sexual dysfunction
Bradycardia and salt and water retention
questions.explanation: Both central α2 agonists cause sedation/dry mouth/sexual dysfunction and bradycardia with fluid retention (A and B); hepatitis/hemolytic anemia/lupus are specific to methyldopa.
questions.keyConcept: Shared central α2-agonist effects of methyldopa and clonidine.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following agent does not act on dopaminergic receptors:
questions.explanation: Dobutamine is a β1 agonist with no dopaminergic activity; dopamine, dopexamine and fenoldopam all act on dopamine receptors.
questions.keyConcept: Dobutamine does not act on dopaminergic receptors.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following agent does not stimulate β1-receptors:
questions.explanation: Per the source key, dopexamine (a β2 and dopaminergic agonist) lacks significant β1 activity. Note: salbutamol is also β2-selective and could be argued — follow the source key.
questions.keyConcept: Dopexamine acts on β2/dopaminergic receptors, not β1.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following agent does not stimulate β2-receptors:
questions.explanation: Dobutamine is a selective β1 agonist with no β2 activity. Ritodrine is a β2 agonist (tocolytic), celiprolol has partial β2-agonist activity, and dopexamine activates β2 receptors.
questions.keyConcept: Dobutamine is β1-selective and lacks β2 activity.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following agent does not stimulate beta1 receptors:
questions.explanation: Dopexamine is a selective beta2 and D1 agonist and does not significantly stimulate beta1 receptors.
questions.keyConcept: Dopexamine acts on beta2 and D1, not beta1.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following agent/s is/are a prodrug:
questions.explanation: Midodrine (→ desglymidodrine) and α-methyldopa (→ α-methylnorepinephrine) are both prodrugs, so C and D.
questions.keyConcept: Midodrine and α-methyldopa are prodrugs.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following are actions mediated by stimulation of alpha1 adrenoceptors except:
options: Relaxation of walls of the GIT and urinary tracts
Decreases potassium release from the liver
Contraction of prostate and vas deferens
questions.explanation: Alpha1 stimulation increases hepatic potassium release through glycogenolysis, it does not decrease it.
questions.keyConcept: Alpha1 stimulation increases hepatic potassium release.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following are actions mediated by stimulation of alpha2 adrenoceptors except:
options: Central sympathetic outflow decreasing blood pressure
questions.explanation: Alpha2 adrenoceptor stimulation inhibits renin release; it does not stimulate it.
questions.keyConcept: Alpha2 stimulation inhibits renin release.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following drug does not act on dopaminergic receptors:
questions.explanation: Dobutamine is a selective beta1 agonist and does not act on dopaminergic receptors.
questions.keyConcept: Dobutamine is beta1-selective, not dopaminergic.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following drugs increase the effect of noradrenaline except:
questions.explanation: Reserpine inhibits vesicular uptake of noradrenaline, depleting its stores and decreasing its effect, unlike the others which enhance it.
questions.keyConcept: Reserpine depletes noradrenaline, reducing its effect.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following indication(s) of adrenaline is/are entirely due to its alpha effect:
options: To prolong the action of local anaesthetics
questions.explanation: Alpha1-mediated vasoconstriction prolongs local anaesthetics and provides topical haemostasis, whereas anaphylaxis and cardiac arrest involve mixed alpha and beta effects.
questions.keyConcept: Adrenaline's vasoconstrictor uses are purely alpha-mediated.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following indication/s of epinephrine is/are entirely due to its α effect:
options: To prolong action of local Anesthetics
questions.explanation: Prolonging local anaesthetic action and stopping epistaxis both rely on α-mediated vasoconstriction; anaphylaxis and cardiac arrest also use β effects.
questions.keyConcept: α-mediated vasoconstriction underlies local-anaesthetic prolongation and epistaxis control.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following is a dual acting sympathomimetic drug:
questions.explanation: Pseudoephedrine is a dual-acting sympathomimetic, stimulating adrenergic receptors both directly and indirectly.
questions.keyConcept: Pseudoephedrine acts both directly and indirectly.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following is a shared adverse effect between dopamine and dobutamine:
questions.explanation: Per the source answer key the marked answer is hypertension; it is most pronounced with higher-dose dopamine through alpha1 agonism.
questions.keyConcept: Dopamine and dobutamine share cardiovascular adverse effects.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following is a wrong statement about adrenaline:
options: Used in asthma due to its alpha and beta agonistic effect
Lifesaving in anaphylactic shock due to its rapid action
Induces hypoglycaemia due to its beta2 agonistic effect
Induces hypotension after injection of an alpha blocker
questions.explanation: Adrenaline induces hyperglycaemia via beta2 stimulation (glycogenolysis and decreased insulin release), not hypoglycaemia.
questions.keyConcept: Adrenaline causes hyperglycaemia, not hypoglycaemia.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following is a wrong statement about amphetamine (a non-catecholamine indirectly acting sympathomimetic):
options: Does not readily cross into the CNS
questions.explanation: Amphetamine is highly lipophilic and readily enters the CNS (a potent central stimulant), so this statement is wrong.
questions.keyConcept: Amphetamine readily crosses into the CNS.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following is a wrong statement about sympathomimetics:
options: Inhibition of vesicular uptake abolishes the effect of indirectly acting drugs
Inhibition of vesicular uptake decreases the effect of dual (mixed) acting drugs
Inhibition of monoamine oxidase increases the effect of indirectly acting drugs
Directly acting alpha1 agonist induces reflex tachycardia
questions.explanation: A directly acting alpha1 agonist causes vasoconstriction and a rise in blood pressure that triggers reflex bradycardia, not tachycardia, so this statement is wrong.
questions.keyConcept: Alpha1 agonists cause reflex bradycardia, not tachycardia.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following is incorrect about subcutaneous administration of adrenaline:
questions.explanation: Adrenaline causes alpha-mediated vasoconstriction and relaxation in the GIT, decreasing (not increasing) GIT motility.
questions.keyConcept: Adrenaline decreases GIT motility.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following is not a character of ephedrine (non-catecholamine sympathomimetic):
options: Not destroyed by MAO and COMT
questions.explanation: Ephedrine is lipophilic and readily enters the CNS, so this statement is incorrect.
questions.keyConcept: Ephedrine readily enters the CNS.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following is not a pharmacological effect of direct acting beta receptor agonists:
options: Relax smooth muscle of the bronchi
questions.explanation: Beta receptor agonists increase heart rate (positive chronotropy) and cardiac output; they do not decrease heart rate.
questions.keyConcept: Beta agonists raise heart rate, not lower it.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following is not a therapeutic use of indirect sympathomimetic (amphetamine):
questions.explanation: Amphetamine can cause hypertension as a side effect and is not used to treat it.
questions.keyConcept: Amphetamine causes, not treats, hypertension.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following is not a therapeutic use of phenylephrine (selective alpha1 agonist):
options: Fundus examination especially in a patient with glaucoma
Paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia with marked hypotension
questions.explanation: Phenylephrine causes vasoconstriction and is not used in peripheral vascular disease, which requires vasodilatation.
questions.keyConcept: Phenylephrine constricts vessels, so it cannot treat vascular disease.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following is not an adverse effect of salbutamol (beta2 agonist):
questions.explanation: Salbutamol causes hypokalaemia, not hyperkalaemia; tremors, reflex tachycardia and worsening hypoxaemia are recognised effects.
questions.keyConcept: Beta2 agonists cause hypokalaemia, not hyperkalaemia.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following is not an adverse effect of selective alpha1 agonist:
questions.explanation: Selective alpha1 agonists cause vasoconstriction with reflex bradycardia, not tachycardia.
questions.keyConcept: Alpha1 agonists cause reflex bradycardia, not tachycardia.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following is not an expected adverse effect of IV infusion of dopamine:
questions.explanation: Dopamine usually causes tachycardia and arrhythmia, not bradycardia.
questions.keyConcept: Dopamine causes tachycardia, not bradycardia.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following is not an expected adverse effect of pseudoephedrine:
options: Urinary retention especially in old males
questions.explanation: Pseudoephedrine causes vasoconstriction and central stimulation; hypotension is not expected, as it tends to raise blood pressure.
questions.keyConcept: Pseudoephedrine raises blood pressure, not lowers it.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following is not an indication for indirect sympathomimetics:
questions.explanation: Indirect sympathomimetics often cause hypertension as an adverse effect and are not used to treat it.
questions.keyConcept: Indirect sympathomimetics cause, not treat, hypertension.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following is not an indication of salbutamol (beta2 agonist):
questions.explanation: Salbutamol is used for asthma and to delay premature labour; it does not treat peripheral vascular disease or chronic postural hypotension (C and D).
questions.keyConcept: Salbutamol does not treat vascular or postural hypotension disorders.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following is not correctly matched to its adverse effect:
options: Clonidine / rebound hypertension even on missing a single dose
Bisoprolol / rebound tachycardia & anginal pain on sudden withdrawal
questions.explanation: Midodrine is an α1 agonist causing hypertension with reflex bradycardia — not hypotension and tachycardia — so D is incorrectly matched.
questions.keyConcept: Midodrine (α1 agonist) causes hypertension with reflex bradycardia.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Tolerance due to prolonged use of salbutamol is due to:
options: Decrease in number of beta2 receptors
questions.explanation: Salbutamol tolerance is multifactorial, involving beta2 receptor down-regulation and changes in lung mechanics ('locked lung syndrome').
questions.keyConcept: Salbutamol tolerance has several contributing mechanisms.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Which of the following can activate dopaminergic as well as adrenergic receptors?
questions.explanation: Dopamine activates dopaminergic (D1), β1 and α1 receptors dose-dependently, and dopexamine activates dopaminergic (D1, D2) and adrenergic β2 receptors. Dobutamine acts only on β1.
questions.keyConcept: Dopamine and dopexamine act on both dopaminergic and adrenergic receptors.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Which of the following has beta action and can be used in bronchial asthma?
questions.explanation: Salbutamol is a selective beta-2 agonist that produces bronchodilation, making it useful in bronchial asthma.
questions.keyConcept: Salbutamol is a beta-2 selective bronchodilator.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Which of the following is a side effect of dopamine?
questions.explanation: Palpitations and anginal pain are common dopamine side effects, especially at higher doses through beta1 stimulation.
questions.keyConcept: Dopamine causes palpitations and anginal pain.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Which of the following is a wrong statement?
options: MAO inhibitors are indicated in parkinsonism
Reserpine depletes stores of noradrenaline and sympathetic outflow
Beta3 agonists relax detrusor muscle and are used in overactive bladder
Dopamine can cross the BBB and is used in Parkinsonism
questions.explanation: Dopamine does not readily cross the blood-brain barrier, so it cannot be used directly in Parkinsonism; levodopa is used instead.
questions.keyConcept: Dopamine cannot cross the BBB to treat Parkinsonism.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Which of the following is a wrong statement?
options: Stimulation of beta1 and beta3 increases lipolysis
Noradrenaline decreases heart rate and increases blood pressure
Adrenaline increases heart rate and decreases blood pressure
Dobutamine is a selective beta1 agonist
Fenoldopam is a selective dopamine receptor agonist
questions.explanation: Adrenaline increases both heart rate and blood pressure (raising mean arterial pressure), so this statement is wrong.
questions.keyConcept: Adrenaline raises both heart rate and blood pressure.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Which of the following is not an indication for indirect sympathomimetics?
questions.explanation: Indirect sympathomimetics are used in narcolepsy, weight reduction and ADHD; they cause hypertension rather than treat it.
questions.keyConcept: Indirect sympathomimetics do not treat hypertension.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Which of the following is the mechanism of action of indirect sympathomimetics?
options: They activate the adrenergic receptor directly
They decrease the degradation of noradrenaline
They activate the down-regulated adrenergic receptor
They increase the release of noradrenaline
questions.explanation: Indirect sympathomimetics, like amphetamine, act mainly by increasing the release of noradrenaline from presynaptic terminals.
questions.keyConcept: Indirect sympathomimetics increase noradrenaline release.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Which of the following is the mechanism of action of reserpine?
options: It blocks uptake I of noradrenaline
It blocks the vesicular uptake of noradrenaline
It is a monoamine oxidase inhibitor
questions.explanation: Reserpine blocks the vesicular uptake of noradrenaline, leading to depletion of noradrenaline stores.
questions.keyConcept: Reserpine blocks vesicular noradrenaline uptake.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Which of the following is wrong regarding mirabegron (beta3 agonist)?
options: May increase the risk of urinary tract infection
May precipitate angioedema in allergic patients
questions.explanation: Mirabegron tends to increase blood pressure and heart rate, so a decrease in blood pressure is incorrect.
questions.keyConcept: Mirabegron raises, not lowers, blood pressure.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Which of the following statement regarding beta adrenergic receptors is not true?
options: Dobutamine is a selective beta1 agonist used in acute heart failure
Salbutamol is a selective beta2 agonist used in acute attacks of bronchial asthma
Beta3 agonist is used in hyperactive bladder with a risk of hypertension
Isoprenaline is a non-selective beta agonist used in treatment of tachycardia
questions.explanation: Isoprenaline is a non-selective beta agonist that causes significant tachycardia, so it is not used to treat tachycardia.
questions.keyConcept: Isoprenaline causes tachycardia and cannot treat it.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Atropine is used in the treatment of organophosphate poisoning. Explain, mentioning its dose.
questions.modelAnswer: Atropine is used to dry bronchial secretions and stop wheezing; it is given as 2-5 mg every 5 minutes until full atropinization is achieved.
questions.keyConcept: Atropine 2-5 mg every 5 min controls muscarinic effects until atropinization.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Compare and contrast between neostigmine and physostigmine.
questions.modelAnswer: Chemical class: neostigmine is a quaternary ammonium compound while physostigmine is a tertiary amine. BBB: neostigmine does not cross the blood-brain barrier while physostigmine does. Routes: neostigmine is given orally or parenterally while physostigmine is given orally, topically (eye) or parenterally. Direct action: neostigmine also has direct nicotinic action on Nm receptors in addition to cholinesterase inhibition while physostigmine is primarily a cholinesterase inhibitor. Clinical use: neostigmine is used for myasthenia gravis, paralytic ileus and as an antidote to neuromuscular blockers, while physostigmine is used for atropine toxicity, glaucoma and (rarely) Alzheimer's disease.
questions.explanation: Their key difference is BBB penetration, which determines their clinical roles.
questions.keyConcept: Neostigmine (quaternary) stays peripheral; physostigmine (tertiary) acts centrally.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Compare between atropine and hyoscine.
questions.modelAnswer: CNS effects: atropine has less CNS penetration and may cause excitement at high doses, while hyoscine penetrates the CNS more and causes drowsiness and amnesia. Antiemetic effect: atropine is weak, while hyoscine is potent (used for motion sickness). Mydriatic duration: atropine is longer acting (days), while hyoscine is shorter acting (hours). Cardiovascular effect: atropine causes more prominent tachycardia, while hyoscine has less pronounced cardiovascular effects.
questions.explanation: Hyoscine is more central and antiemetic; atropine is more cardiac and longer-acting on the eye.
questions.keyConcept: Hyoscine is more sedating/antiemetic; atropine is more tachycardic and longer mydriatic.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Complete the following statements about cholinergic and anticholinergic drugs.
questions.modelAnswer: Edrophonium is used in the diagnosis of myasthenia gravis. Donepezil is the neostigmine analogue used in Alzheimer dementia. The effect of atropine on the eye persists for more than 72 hours. Atropine is contraindicated in acute glaucoma and benign prostatic hyperplasia. Pilocarpine is the drug of choice in the treatment of glaucoma, while bethanechol is the drug of choice in megacolon.
questions.keyConcept: Edrophonium diagnoses myasthenia, donepezil treats Alzheimer's, and atropine is contraindicated in glaucoma/BPH.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Discuss the pharmacological effect of atropine on the CNS and eye and their clinical implications.
questions.modelAnswer: CNS: at low doses minimal effects; at higher doses it causes restlessness, disorientation, confusion, hallucinations and even delirium and mania. Clinical implication: can be useful (e.g. in some Parkinsonian symptoms) but is often a dose-limiting adverse effect, especially in the elderly who are prone to delirium. Eye: causes mydriasis by paralysing the sphincter pupillae and cycloplegia by paralysing the ciliary muscle. Clinical implication: mydriasis is used for fundus examination, but in eyes with narrow anterior chambers it can precipitate acute angle-closure glaucoma; cycloplegia causes blurred near vision.
questions.explanation: Antimuscarinic CNS and ocular effects are both therapeutic and hazardous.
questions.keyConcept: Atropine causes central excitation and ocular mydriasis/cycloplegia with key risks.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Enumerate 4 adverse effects of cholinomimetics.
questions.modelAnswer: Gastrointestinal: nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, abdominal cramps, increased salivation. Cardiovascular: bradycardia, hypotension, AV block. Respiratory: bronchospasm and increased bronchial secretions. Ocular: miosis, blurred vision, frontal headache. Genitourinary: urinary urgency and frequency.
questions.explanation: Adverse effects mirror excess muscarinic stimulation across organ systems.
questions.keyConcept: Cholinomimetics cause GI, cardiac, respiratory and ocular muscarinic effects.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Enumerate the drugs which block cholinergic actions.
questions.modelAnswer: Cholinergic actions are blocked by antimuscarinic drugs, neuromuscular blockers, ganglion blockers and botulinum toxins.
questions.keyConcept: Antimuscarinics, neuromuscular and ganglion blockers, and botulinum toxin block cholinergic actions.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Enumerate the pharmacological actions of local eye application of atropine.
questions.modelAnswer: Mydriasis: pupil dilatation from blockade of M3 receptors on the sphincter pupillae muscle. Cycloplegia: paralysis of accommodation from blockade of M3 receptors on the ciliary muscle. Increased intraocular pressure: especially in narrow-angle glaucoma, by impairing aqueous humour outflow. Decreased lacrimation: reduced tear production leading to dry eyes.
questions.explanation: Atropine blocks ocular muscarinic receptors, affecting pupil, lens and tears.
questions.keyConcept: Ocular atropine causes mydriasis, cycloplegia, raised IOP and dry eyes.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Enumerate the therapeutic uses of neostigmine.
questions.modelAnswer: Neostigmine is used in myasthenia gravis and as an antidote to non-depolarizing neuromuscular blockers such as curare.
